newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Railcorp sees higher '97 results.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Railcorp sees higher '97 results.

text.p: Pioneer Railcorp, a freight short-line holding company with 15 railraods in nine states, said it expects improved earnings in 1997.

"We have returned to the profitability that we enjoyed for the 19 consecutive quarters prior to the end of 1996," Guy Brendman, chairman, said in a statement. "With the severe weather behind us and grain and lumber shipments increasing along with steel and food, we fully expect to increase both sales and earnings during 1997."
In 1996 it had net income of $102,145 or $0.02 a share on operating revenues of $11.0 million
Earlier today, it reported a drop in first quarter income to $0.02 a share from $0.04 a year ago, which it attributed to severe weather conditions.

The company said winter snow storms and spring flooding led to decreases in grain shipments during the quarter. Adverse weather in the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997 made its Minnesota Central line virtually inoperable, it added.
Revenues in the quarter rose to $2.8 million from $2.5 million a year ago due to strong performances by three short lines acquired last year and by one of its older lines.
